AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sign shows that compost is ready? (1 mark)
   A. It is wet and smells sour
   B. It is dark, crumbly and smells like fresh earth
   C. It is hot and full of whole peelings
   D. It is grey and hard

2. What is compost manure? (1 mark)
   A. Fertiliser made in a factory
   B. A dark crumbly material made when plant and animal wastes rot
   C. A kind of animal feed
   D. Fresh soil from a river bank

3. Which statement about a three-stone fire is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It saves the most fuel
   B. It never needs firewood
   C. It loses a lot of heat to the air
   D. It is completely smoke-free

4. Which is a problem of cutting many trees for firewood? (1 mark)
   A. More rain falls at once
   B. Trees grow faster
   C. Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
   D. The soil becomes richer

5. Why should you prepare all the food before lighting the fire? (1 mark)
   A. So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
   B. To use more wood
   C. To cook faster than a cooker
   D. To make the food colder

6. How is charcoal made? (1 mark)
   A. By drying maize
   B. By burning wood slowly with little air
   C. By mixing soil and water
   D. By boiling water

7. What should you do with the fire when cooking is finished? (1 mark)
   A. Add more wood
   B. Leave it burning
   C. Put it out
   D. Pour paraffin on it

8. How can a family get firewood without destroying forests? (1 mark)
   A. Cut young trees only
   B. Burn grass
   C. Cut trees from forests at night
   D. Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut

9. Which crop is likely to be eaten by birds? (1 mark)
   A. Compost
   B. Rocks
   C. Firewood
   D. Ripening millet

10. What is a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of fence
   B. A wild bird
   C. A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
   D. A farm tool for digging

11. Why do we cover the seeds with a thin layer of fine soil? (1 mark)
   A. To protect them and keep them moist
   B. To let birds find them
   C. To make them bigger
   D. To stop them growing

12. How can a person without a garden grow tiny-seeded crops? (1 mark)
   A. On a road
   B. On hard rock
   C. In a container seedbed with drainage holes
   D. Only in a forest

13. Which crop is established by direct sowing of tiny seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Sweet potato
   B. Mango
   C. Banana
   D. Carrot

14. Why do we label the seedbed rows? (1 mark)
   A. To remember the crop and the date sown
   B. To scare birds
   C. To decorate
   D. To give plants names

15. Which is likely to take longest to give fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Passion fruit
   B. Radish
   C. Pawpaw
   D. Mango tree

16. Which of these fruits does best in cool highland areas? (1 mark)
   A. Tree tomato
   B. Mango
   C. Coconut
   D. Cashew nut

17. Why should the soil be firmed around a newly planted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To dry the roots
   C. To remove air spaces and hold the roots
   D. To make the plant fall

18. How does eating fruit help our health? (1 mark)
   A. It stops us drinking water
   B. It gives only sugar and nothing else
   C. It gives vitamins and fibre
   D. It makes us weak

19. Which is a pest problem for ripe fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Sun
   B. Stones
   C. Sand
   D. Fruit flies and birds

20. Which nutrient do oranges and guavas supply in large amounts? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Starch
   C. Salt
   D. Vitamin C

21. What is a tree tomato? (1 mark)
   A. A vegetable that grows underground
   B. A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
   C. A climbing vine
   D. A cereal

22. Which animal browses on leaves and shoots from bushes? (1 mark)
   A. Duck
   B. Rabbit only
   C. Hen
   D. Goat

23. What is the meat of sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Mutton
   B. Bacon
   C. Pork
   D. Beef

24. Which fruit is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Ugali
   B. Rice
   C. Mango
   D. Chapati

25. What is one way to choose foods for a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Pick one or more foods from each group
   B. Pick only sweet food
   C. Pick only cheap food
   D. Pick only your favourite food

26. Why do we crack an egg into a bowl first? (1 mark)
   A. To check it and remove bits of shell
   B. To make it hot
   C. To make it grow
   D. To cook it

27. What is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Storing food
   B. Cutting food
   C. Preparing food using heat
   D. Washing food

28. Why should you wear clean clothes? (1 mark)
   A. To make the clothes wear out
   B. Dirty clothes can carry germs and smell
   C. To save water
   D. To get tired

29. About how long should you rub hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. About 20 seconds
   B. Not at all
   C. About 5 minutes
   D. About 1 second

30. Which method removes dry dirt from the floor with a broom? (1 mark)
   A. Dusting
   B. Mopping
   C. Washing
   D. Sweeping

31. Why should dusters and mops be washed after use? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavy
   B. To make them smell
   C. So they wear out
   D. So they do not spread dirt and germs

32. Which is a way of reducing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Reuse containers
   B. Buy more packages
   C. Throw things away quickly
   D. Burn tins

33. Why is a damp cloth used for dusting? (1 mark)
   A. It traps the dust
   B. It hides dust
   C. It scatters the dust
   D. It dries the room

34. What should you do with laces when cleaning canvas shoes? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them dirty
   B. Burn them
   C. Remove and wash them separately
   D. Cut them

35. Which PPE keeps dust from being breathed in? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Gumboots
   C. Headgear
   D. Overall

36. What should you do after cleaning PPE? (1 mark)
   A. Wipe them on clothes
   B. Eat without washing
   C. Wash your hands with soap
   D. Play in mud

37. Which kind of PPE is suitable for handling compost? (1 mark)
   A. A dress only
   B. Gloves and gumboots
   C. Shorts only
   D. A necktie

38. What is the use of a scarecrow shirt made with tacking? (1 mark)
   A. It clothes the scarecrow using stitches
   B. It is eaten
   C. It waters plants
   D. It is a tool

39. Which skill from Mathematics helps in tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Naming shapes only
   B. Measuring
   C. Adding money
   D. Telling time

40. Why should tacking thread not be pulled tight? (1 mark)
   A. Thread is expensive
   B. It will become long
   C. It will not hold
   D. The cloth will wrinkle

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why tacking thread should be loose. (2 marks)

42. Describe how to make a tippy tap. (4 marks)

43. Plan a group project of making a scarecrow shirt using tacking. Give materials, steps, safety and how the group shares work. (5 marks)

44. State three safety rules when cleaning PPE. (3 marks)

45. How should cloth items such as overalls and cloth masks be cleaned? (3 marks)

46. Give three signs that fruit is ripe, naming the fruit. (3 marks)

47. Name three small wild animals that destroy crops. (3 marks)

48. Give two advantages of direct sowing. (2 marks)

49. Write the steps for growing carrots from seed to harvest. (5 marks)

50. Give three times when you should wash your hands. (3 marks)

51. How can you tell that compost is ready for use? (3 marks)

52. Describe how a group can share the work of growing a fruit tree at school. (4 marks)

53. Explain how measuring skills help you in tacking. (3 marks)

54. Give three ways of disposing of refuse safely. (3 marks)

55. Describe how to care for a seedbed after sowing. (4 marks)

56. List four basic needs of domestic animals. (4 marks)

57. Describe how to build a compost heap using layers. (4 marks)

58. Why should gumboots not be dried near a hot fire? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — It is dark, crumbly and smells like fresh earth
   Ready compost looks and smells like soil and the materials cannot be recognised.

2. B — A dark crumbly material made when plant and animal wastes rot
   Compost is organic manure made from rotted wastes.

3. C — It loses a lot of heat to the air
   Open fires waste heat.

4. C — Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
   Trees protect soil and water, so cutting them harms the environment.

5. A — So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
   Fuel is not wasted waiting.

6. B — By burning wood slowly with little air
   Charcoal is wood partly burnt in limited air.

7. C — Put it out
   Leaving fire burning wastes fuel and is dangerous.

8. D — Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
   Growing trees keeps a supply of wood.

9. D — Ripening millet
   Birds eat ripening grain such as millet and sorghum.

10. C — A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
   A scarecrow frightens away birds and other animals.

11. A — To protect them and keep them moist
   Covering helps seeds germinate.

12. C — In a container seedbed with drainage holes
   A box or tin with holes and fine soil works well.

13. D — Carrot
   Carrots are sown directly because transplanting damages their roots.

14. A — To remember the crop and the date sown
   Labels prevent confusion.

15. D — Mango tree
   Big trees like mango take several years.

16. A — Tree tomato
   Tree tomato grows well in cooler highlands, while coconut, cashew and mango like warm places.

17. C — To remove air spaces and hold the roots
   Air pockets dry out roots.

18. C — It gives vitamins and fibre
   Fruits protect the body and help digestion.

19. D — Fruit flies and birds
   Ripe fruit attracts flies and birds.

20. D — Vitamin C
   Citrus fruits and guavas are rich in vitamin C.

21. B — A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
   Tree tomato is a woody tree fruit.

22. D — Goat
   Goats browse on shrubs.

23. A — Mutton
   Mutton is sheep meat.

24. C — Mango
   Mango has vitamins.

25. A — Pick one or more foods from each group
   A balanced meal includes all three groups.

26. A — To check it and remove bits of shell
   You avoid a bad egg spoiling the pan.

27. C — Preparing food using heat
   Cooking uses heat to make food safe and tasty.

28. B — Dirty clothes can carry germs and smell
   Clean clothes keep us fresh.

29. A — About 20 seconds
   This is long enough to clean properly.

30. D — Sweeping
   Sweeping uses a broom.

31. D — So they do not spread dirt and germs
   Dirty tools spread dirt.

32. A — Reuse containers
   Reuse cuts down rubbish.

33. A — It traps the dust
   Damp cloths hold dust.

34. C — Remove and wash them separately
   Laces need to be washed too.

35. A — Dust mask
   A mask covers the nose and mouth.

36. C — Wash your hands with soap
   Hands can carry germs.

37. B — Gloves and gumboots
   They protect hands and feet.

38. A — It clothes the scarecrow using stitches
   Tacking holds the shirt pieces together.

39. B — Measuring
   Measuring gives even and accurate stitches.

40. D — The cloth will wrinkle
   Loose stitches lie flat.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Tight thread pulls and wrinkles the cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for pulls, 1 mark for wrinkles.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Take a clean jerrican; make a small hole near the cap; hang it; tie a string from the cap to a foot lever; place a basin below and hang soap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: old cloth, needles, thread, scissors, chalk, ruler. Steps: measure and cut two pieces; pin; tack along sides; leave openings; sew firmly; stuff. Safety: count needles. Group: share tools, assign jobs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark materials, 2 marks steps, 1 mark safety, 1 mark teamwork.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use soap and clean water; keep buckets and brushes from small children; wash your hands after; clean in an open place with drainage.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash with soap and water, rinse well and dry in the sun to help kill germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Passion fruit turns purple or yellow and wrinkles; guava turns yellowish and smells sweet; pawpaw turns yellow or orange and gives when pressed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with fruit.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds, hares, squirrels, monkeys (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct animal.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Roots are not disturbed, no nursery is needed, saves time and work (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare a fine seedbed; make drills about 1 cm deep; sow seeds thinly with sand; cover and water gently; thin to about 5 cm; weed and water; harvest after three to four months by loosening the soil and pulling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before eating, after using the toilet, after playing outside, after touching animals, after coughing (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is dark brown, crumbly, smells like earth, and the original wastes cannot be seen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sign.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a chart with jobs such as watering, weeding, mulching and recording; take turns each week; check the plant daily; record dates of flowers and fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity or arrangement.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Measuring gives correct stitch lengths, straight lines and correct size of the item.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Compost organic waste; put other waste in a bin with a lid and take it to a collection point; reuse or recycle paper, plastic and glass; wrap broken glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water gently and regularly, remove weeds, thin the seedlings, and protect the bed from animals and birds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean water, enough feed, clean shelter, health care and kind handling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each need.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a shady place; lay sticks; add a dry layer, a green layer and dung; sprinkle soil and water; repeat to chest height; cover the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for place, base and layers, soil and water, and covering.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Heat can crack the rubber and spoil the boots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for heat, 1 mark for cracking.
